title: Immediate-fix decision tree and branching contract for LTS & rolling releases
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We lack a single, actionable decision tree and explicit branching contract for when an issue merits an immediate production patch vs queued point release. This causes inconsistent triage, delayed mitigations for high-impact regressions on LTS channels, and confusion about backport obligations across teams.

Goal: Produce a concise runbook and automated checks that cover: severity criteria, branching strategy (patch branches and naming), backport matrix for supported releases (LTS and rolling), rollout gate checklist (health signals + time-based rollback triggers), and developer/operator responsibilities during a hot-fix flow. The runbook will be short (1–2 pages) and wired into our Pager/Slack automation and PR templates.

Scope: Runtime and serving infra only (service mesh, model-serving runtime, autoscaler, KV cache, kernel selection). Excludes docs for client SDKs.

Deliverables:
- Decision tree diagram + triage rubric (severity definitions S0-S3 mapped to actions)
- Branching contract: branch name patterns (e.g., release/1.20-patch/<semver>), tagging policy, and CI gate exceptions for emergency patches
- Backport matrix: table of supported releases, minimum patch level to accept backport, and required reviewers per release tier
- Rollout gates checklist: pre-rollout health checks, canary percent schedule, automated monitors + rollback triggers, post-rollback communication template
- Automation: PR template, GitHub Actions workflow to create patch branches and open backport PRs, Slack alert template for triage channel
- Runbook artifact uploaded to Confluence and linked in Incident Response playbook

Key decisions to make in this ticket:
1) Severity thresholds: define S0 (catastrophic data loss/security), S1 (major outage for paid customers), S2 (degraded service with workaround), S3 (non-urgent bug). Decide which severities require immediate patch branch creation vs scheduled point release.
2) Backport policy: how many patch levels back do we support for LTS and rolling channels; e.g., LTS: last 3 minor releases; rolling: last 1 minor.
3) Release numbering: whether emergency patches use an appended build metadata token (e.g., 1.20.3+hotfix20250304) or increase patch semver.
4) Approval model: who must approve a patch PR for each release tier (oncall, release manager, security for S0)

Risks and constraints:
- Backporting across major refactors may be technically infeasible — we need an explicit 'cannot backport' path that updates the matrix and customer comms.
- CI time for running full test suites on older branches; propose targeted test matrix and optional longer-running job for post-merge verification.

Success criteria:
- A runbook merged and signed off by release manager and head of infra by due_date
- Automated PR creation workflow lives in repo and creates correct branch + backport PRs during simulated incident drill
- Oncall runbook references the new decision tree and uses Slack template during drills

Notes & links:
- Confluence draft: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/l/cp/XYz123 (draft, will be updated)
- Spike PR for branch tooling: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4872
- Incident postmortem example with manual backport: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AbC-example

Open questions:
- Do we want mandatory binary-built artifacts for patches (to ensure reproducible build) or allow source-only patch PRs for low-risk changes?
- Which metrics are minimum gate signals for canary success (latency p95, error rate, 5xx rate, token-drop rate)?

Next steps:
- Runbook draft v0.1 created and linked to this ticket (Confluence).
- Schedule working session with Release Manager and Platform SRE: 2025-02-25.
- Implement minimal GitHub Action to scaffold patch branch + PR template (owner: infra, ETA 1 week).
comments: 2025-02-21 — Aisha Kapoor: Drafted initial decision tree and uploaded to Confluence. Added recommended severity mapping and branching patterns. Seeking input from Release Manager (Lena Chen) and Security (Marco Ruiz).

2025-02-24 — Diego Morales: Ran a small spike to create release/1.20-patch/1.20.2 branch from tag v1.20.2; workflow created branch and opened PR template automatically (see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4872). Tests require adjustments for older-commit build steps.

2025-02-27 — Lena Chen (Release Manager): Feedback — prefer incrementing semver patch (1.20.3) for clarity in customer dashboards rather than build metadata. Also: require release manager + oncall signoff for S1, security required for S0. Added to decision tree.

2025-03-03 — Security (Marco Ruiz): S0 (data loss/secret exposure) must block automatic backport; patch PRs must include an HSM/KMS review when key management code touched. Flagging examples where backports were rejected due to incompatible KMS SDK versions.

2025-03-06 — Diego Morales: Implemented CI job that runs minimal test matrix for patch branches (unit + critical integration smoke). Full test suite is optional post-merge. Drafting Slack templates and Alert runbook for triage channel.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runbook merged in Confluence with reviewers: Release Manager, Head of Infra, Security. 2) GitHub Action scaffolding creates branch+PR consistently in a dry-run. 3) At least one simulated S1 drill performs automated branch creation, canary rollout, and rollback using new checklist. 4) Backport matrix published and linked from release notes.
